text: Newson, Three Mariners Inn,” and handed the packet to Elizabeth. “Deliver it to her personally, please,” said Henchard. “Well, I am glad to see you here, Elizabeth-Jane—very glad. We must have a long talk together—but not just now.” He took her hand at parting, and held it so warmly that she, who had known so little friendship, was much affected, and tears rose to her aerial-grey eyes. The instant that she was gone Henchard’s state showed itself more distinctly; having shut the door he sat in his dining-room stiffly erect, gazing at the opposite wall as if he read his history there.
